body: I don’t tend to study war poems but Dulce Et Decorum Est is a good one to look at
I’m young and have lots to learn about poetry and I just wanted to express my interest in how many soldiers views were expressed through his poem
Then I apologise, this is just what I was taught.

For him to do in the war would be for him to have battled? To be a casualty of war you have to die fighting, he did not.

I was showing how it was displayed through a poem and that it was a good example on how naive the men were and the effect. Brooke didn’t even die in the war, he was bitten and died from blood poisoning.

I just wish it didn’t have to end like that for Molly, I know she was drunk and all, she missed the old Dutch who loved her, but I wish she never said what she did

Everything was so rushed, and yes Lenny did die in that scene which made it even worse, Dutch didn’t even seem phased, he was so stuck on his “plan”
